method: Read from the release file by Claude Opus 5.5: the zotero://zoteroaddoncollection handler, its execJS action, verifySignature and importKey, and the public key it verifies against; searched the bundle for a private key.
label: A zotero:// link (a web page can open one) can make it run code its developer signed, without asking you
summary: Its zotero://zoteroaddoncollection link runs JavaScript only when the link carries a signature that matches a public key written into the plugin, so only someone holding the developer's private key can make one; that key isn't in the plugin. Nothing in a signed link expires, so any web page can reopen a link the developer signed once, and the developer can run code in your Zotero without releasing a new version.

facts.handler: zotero://zoteroaddoncollection, registered at startup (registerConfigScheme in onStartup); actions configSource, install and execJS
facts.check: execJS verifies an RSA-PSS (SHA-256, salt 64) signature over the base64 source against publicKeyBase64, an RSA public key written into the plugin, and throws before running anything if it fails
facts.runs: new AsyncFunction(source) with Zotero's full privileges, no prompt
facts.replay: the signature covers only the source: no expiry, nonce or origin check, so a signed link can be reopened by any page
facts.notes: encryptExecJsCommand(source, privateKey) is the developer's signing helper; it takes the private key as an argument and no PEM private key or pkcs8 key material appears in the bundle. The install action (handleInstall) is the separate installs-addons finding.
